title: Indian Physiography: The Six Faces of the Subcontinent

questions.question: Which is the correct order of Himalayan ranges from north to south?
questions.rationale: The Greater Himalayas (Himadri) lie on the Tibetan side, then the Lesser Himalayas (Himachal), and the outermost Shiwaliks towards the plains.

questions.question: The Himalayas were formed by:
options: Collision of the Indian plate with the Eurasian plate, closing the Tethys Sea
questions.rationale: Continental collision folded the Tethys sediments upward; the Indian plate still pushes ~5 cm/year, keeping the range rising and seismically active.

questions.question: The porous, pebbly belt at the Himalayan foot where streams disappear underground is the:
questions.rationale: Bhabar is the 8–16 km porous strip at the mountain foot; streams re-emerge in the marshy Terai to its south.

questions.question: The Peninsular Plateau is divided into the Central Highlands and the Deccan Plateau by which feature?
questions.rationale: The Narmada rift valley separates the Central Highlands (north) from the Deccan Plateau (south), both parts of the ancient Gondwana core.

questions.question: The highest peak entirely within India, Anai Mudi (2,695 m), stands in the:
questions.rationale: Anai Mudi crowns the Western Ghats (Sahyadri) in Kerala — the Eastern Ghats' highest is Mahendragiri (1,501 m).

questions.question: The Thar Desert lies mainly arid because:
options: It is far from the sea
The Aravalli ranges block moisture-bearing winds
It lies in a rain shadow of the Western Ghats
questions.rationale: The relict Aravallis intercept what moisture reaches Rajasthan; combined with high aridity and sandy soils, rainfall stays under ~150 mm/year.

questions.question: Which correctly matches the coastal plains?
options: West: narrow with lagoons; East: broad and deltaic
questions.rationale: The western plain is narrow (10–50 km) with lagoons like Vembanad, while the eastern plain (100–130 km) carries the Mahanadi–Godavari–Krishna–Kaveri deltas.

questions.question: Lakshadweep islands are:
questions.rationale: Lakshadweep is a chain of coral atolls on the Laccadive–Chagos ridge; volcanic origin belongs to the Andaman & Nicobar group (Barren Island is India's only active volcano).

questions.question: The western coastal plain is widest and characterised by tidal mudflats and salt marshes in:
questions.rationale: In Gujarat the plain broadens around the gulfs of Kachchh and Khambhat with extensive mudflats — Rann of Kachchh — unlike the narrow Konkan and Malabar stretches.

questions.question: The Deccan Plateau's extensive black-soil tracts come from:
questions.rationale: Cretaceous–Eocene basaltic lava flows weathered into moisture-retentive black regur soils — ideal for cotton — over much of Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh.
